goal: Postgres pool acquisition has a bounded wait and a pool-exhaustion timeout surfaces as a TRANSIENT-classified, retryable failure within that bound instead of an uncaught PoolTimeout.

relevant: packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/store_postgres.py -- the pool is built with only min/max size (~line 201); add a bounded acquisition wait and classify the timeout
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_claims_postgres.py -- the claim-store pool (~line 201) needs the same bound applied in this same change
packages/flywheel-core/tests/test_store_postgres.py -- add pool_acquire_bounded; it must skip cleanly when no Postgres test container is available, matching the existing gating in this file
constraints: Reuse the TRANSIENT classification from transient-classifier-backoff; a pool-acquisition timeout classifies TRANSIENT and retryable
Both the core store pool (store_postgres.py) and the claim store pool (_claims_postgres.py) get the bounded wait in this same change -- they share the pool-construction shape

pool_acquire_bounded: with the pool exhausted (all connections held) a competing acquire must return/raise a TRANSIENT-classified failure within the configured timeout, asserted with a wall-time upper bound generous to CI
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done
non_goals: Do not modify files under tests/ except adding the named test; do not weaken existing postgres-store tests
Do not set the timeout so high the test passes by never timing out -- the failure must occur within a finite bound
Do not leave the timeout unclassified (an unclassified PoolTimeout would still be treated as fatal by the breaker)
edge_cases: No Postgres container present -> the test skips, it does not fail
An unbounded acquire that blocks forever must fail the wall-time upper-bound assertion
